## Pull request overview

This PR fixes CI failures in `@object-ui/fields` caused by a Rules of Hooks violation (hooks declared after an early return) and strict TypeScript errors from implicit `any` callback parameters. It unblocks the `fields` package build, preventing downstream Turbo pipeline failures.

**Changes:**
- Moved derived values and `useCallback` hooks above the `readonly` early return to satisfy `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks`.
- Added explicit `string` parameter annotations in `accept.split(',').map(...)` / `.some(...)` callbacks to satisfy `TS7006` under `strict: true`.
- Repositioned the `readonly` rendering block after hook declarations while preserving read-only rendering behavior.

`fileField` is typed as `any`, so `accept` is inferred as `any` (`fileField.accept.join(',')` returns `any`). If you narrow/cast `fileField.accept` to `string[]`, `accept` becomes `string | undefined` and you can drop the extra `(t: string)` annotations while keeping strict typing intact.

The readonly rendering path uses `readonlyFiles.map((file: any, …)` and then reads `file.name` / `file.original_name`. Consider introducing a small `FileValue` type (with optional `name`, `original_name`, etc.) and using it here (and in the non-readonly list) to avoid `any` and keep strict typing meaningful.
